description: Collect a category from any of twelve marketplaces and read it: products with prices, star histograms, the review text itself, and the arithmetic over them (price spread, rating spread, which aspects recur across how many brands, and the share of each product's ratings sitting at 1-2 stars). `marketplace` picks the site — one of amazon, aliexpress, cdiscount, flipkart, mercadolibre, lazada, otto, rakuten, trendyol, jumia, vinted, temu. Pass `query` to search the category, `items` to pin named competitors by id or URL, or both. You write the read: purchase drivers, barriers, what the incumbents do well, the gaps, and how a new entrant could position. Costs 3 nooticr credits per product collected — a product with reviews is a real browser render behind the site's bot defences. Collection runs in the background: this returns everything ready within `waitSeconds` plus a scanId to continue with marketplace_scan_status, which is free and worth repeating until the scan is done. Never conclude, or end your turn, on an incomplete scan: a read of 4 of 10 listings presented as the category is wrong. For Amazon specifically, scan_amazon_category returns the same shape plus Amazon's own review-aspect counts. Use for a category or a competitive set on one of these marketplaces; get_marketplace_product reads one product.

domain.description: Amazon only: the marketplace host, e.g. www.amazon.co.uk. Other sites use `market`.

focus.description: An extra question to answer from the reviews, e.g. 'what do buyers say about sizing?'

items.description: Named competitors, by product id or URL. Amazon: an ASIN or a full Amazon product URL · AliExpress: the numeric id from /item/<id>.html, or a full AliExpress product URL · Cdiscount: the SKU from a product URL's /f-<category>-<sku>.html, or the full URL · Flipkart: the 16-character PID from a product URL's pid= parameter, or the full URL · Mercado Libre: a site id such as MLA904253674, or a full Mercado Libre product URL · Lazada: the number after -i in a product URL (13711387806 in /products/<slug>-i13711387806.html), or the full URL · Otto: the tail of the product path — C1720803139 on otto.de, or the SKU AKLBB2029107352 on ottoversand.at · Rakuten: on Ichiba `<shopId>_<itemId>` (411453_10000003) or `<shop>/<manageNumber>`; on Taiwan `<shop>/<productCode>`. A full product URL works too · Trendyol: the number after -p- in a product URL (819066262 in /brand/name-p-819066262), or the full URL · Jumia: a SKU such as OR537EA86PWGTNAFAMZ. A product URL does NOT contain it — the number at the end of a product path is a different handle — so reach a product through `query` instead · Vinted: the numeric id from /items/<id>, or a full Vinted item URL · Temu: the goods id after -g- in a product URL, or the full URL

market.description: The storefront to read, for the sites that have more than one. Amazon: a country code or host — com (US), co.uk, de, fr, it, es, ca, co.jp, in, com.br, com.mx, com.au, nl, se, pl, com.be, com.tr, ae, sa, eg, sg, cn. Default www.amazon.com · Mercado Libre: one of eighteen markets, named however it comes to hand — MLB, br, Brazil or mercadolivre.com.br. Inferred from the ids when omitted, and a job runs against one market: an id from another is refused rather than mis-filed · Lazada: sg, my, th, vn, ph or id. An item id is scoped to one of them — the same id on another Lazada host is a different product or nothing at all · Otto: de or at. The two are not interchangeable: an id from one does not address a product on the other · Rakuten: jp (Ichiba) or tw. Taiwan publishes no review text, so a category study there reads on price and rating alone · Trendyol: one of 47 storefronts — tr, de, ae, sa, at, be, fr, it, nl, pl, ro and the rest. An id is scoped to one: the same number 404s on another country's · Jumia: ng, eg, ke, ma, ci, gh, sn, tn, ug or dz · Vinted: one of 27 European storefronts — fr, de, es, it, pl, co.uk, com (US), com.au and the rest. A listing belongs to exactly one: the same item id does not exist on another country's Vinted · AliExpress, Cdiscount, Flipkart, Temu have one storefront each and take no market argument.

marketplace.description: Which site to read. One of: amazon, aliexpress, cdiscount, flipkart, mercadolibre, lazada, otto, rakuten, trendyol, jumia, vinted, temu.

query.description: Category or keyword to search, e.g. 'cast iron skillet'. Two to four words, the common name a shopper would type rather than a catalogue description, and no quotes or AND/OR — none of these sites read them as operators, they search for them and narrow to nothing. It has to be in the storefront's language — Amazon: the storefront's own — English on com, co.uk, ca, in, com.au and sg, otherwise the country's · AliExpress: English · Cdiscount: French · Flipkart: English · Mercado Libre: Spanish, except Brazil (MLB), which is Portuguese · Lazada: English on sg and ph; Thai, Vietnamese, Indonesian or Malay on th, vn, id and my · Otto: German, on both storefronts · Rakuten: Japanese on jp, Traditional Chinese on tw · Trendyol: Turkish on tr; the storefront's own language elsewhere · Jumia: English on ng, ke, gh and ug; French on ci, sn, ma, tn and dz; Arabic or French on eg · Vinted: the storefront's own — French on fr, German on de, Polish on pl, and so on · Temu: English. A query in the wrong language does not fail: it returns a few imported listings, which reads as a thin category and is really a bad search. Brand names are not translated. A scan that came back with no products is a reason to change the query, not to raise the limit.

reviews.description: Collect review text too (default true). False is faster and much cheaper to run, but leaves only the aggregates.

waitSeconds.description: How long to wait before returning partial results (default 45, max 55). Capped under the 60s at which hosts abandon a tool call — asking for longer returns nothing and loses the scanId, not a bigger answer. Poll marketplace_scan_status for the rest instead; it is free and repeatable.

name: scan_marketplace_category

complete.description: False means more listings are still coming.

market.description: The storefront this ran against, however the site names it.

cached.description: true when the answer was served from the server's cache, at no cost.

charged.description: false when the call was refused before anything was debited.

nextCall.description: Set while the scan is still collecting: call this next, and write no conclusion until it is null.

reviewSummary.description: Amazon's own digest of the reviews.

reviewsGated.description: True when Amazon withheld the review bodies behind sign-in.

reviews.description: Every review across the scan, worst-rated first — the barriers are the half a summary drops.

groups.description: Brands (or sellers) holding the ratings counted.

priceIqr.description: Price spread; null with fewer than four prices.

top3SharePct.description: Share of the ratings held by the top three; null with fewer than three.

unitsAvailable.description: Always false: rating counts are not units sold.

competition.description: Competitive intensity from rating counts: concentration and price spread, never units or revenue.

rollup.description: The arithmetic over the set: price and rating spread, aspects by brand, 1-2 star share, competition.

scanId.description: Pass to amazon_scan_status to pick a running collection back up.
